title: Drummers as blood brothers and other dancers of the day
summary: Green says tap dancer and drummer are blood brothers, and lists Roland James, Baby Lawrence, Groundhog, Taps Miller and novelty dancers like George Rochette.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, what was the tap dancer's relationship with the drummer, for example?

Well, they were what they call blood brothers, because the drummer played the rhythm for the music of the band, and the tap dancer is all rhythm, see. So, it's as simple as that. That's the relation to the drummer, you see. Like, you had the tempo by the drums, you see.
We're into the -- what would you say, the late '30's now?
No, I'd say early '40's, '41, '42, like that.
And who are the -- what other dancers

Well, most of the greats they had -- Roland James of Sonny and Sonny, Sonny Austin of the Four (Unintelligible) and Baby Lawrence of the Harlem Highlanders. Well, then, Groundhog -- he was coming out of retirement at another time -- at that time. Because he had been a popular dancer with the Whitman sisters. And then you had Taps Miller -- that was the tap dancing trumpet player. He composed songs like, 'Wham, rebop, boom, bam, I'm killer-diller, yes I am. Wham, bebop, boom, bam, I can sing and I can jam.' And he would tap dance and he'd play the trumpet, you know. dancers began Tap dance was beginning to like variate you see, they tried to add a little different characters to their routines, you know. George Rochette used to come out with three dishes and he'd turn them upside down and he would tap dance on the three dishes, see. That was known as novelty tap.
Let me ask you, did novelty tap start prior to this particular era, which is the big band era? Were there novelty acts?
Oh, yes, yeah. Will Mahoney was a novelty act by dancing on the marimba, see, and --
